marker_weekday_counted_ambiguous: "nedelja" names both the weekday Sunday and, in some sources, the week
(see weekday_6.voc) -- a COUNT immediately before it ("dve nedelja", "10
nedelja") can only be a span of weeks, since nobody counts specific
Sundays that way, but this locale ships no week duration unit under
"nedelja" (sedmica is the unambiguous week word; unit_week.voc/
unit1_week.voc). Answering the lone-Sunday sub-reading and stranding the
count would be a worse wrong answer than none, so the count vetoes the
weekday match instead of asserting the unsourced week reading. Wiktionary,
"nedelje" is the paucal (2-4) GENITIVE SINGULAR of the same noun --
unit_week.voc's own "sedmica"/"sedmice" pair uses that exact case for a
counted week ("dve sedmice"), so "dve nedelje" is read the same way and
needs the same veto the nominative gets above. Wiktionary, nedelja,
marker_weekday_week_ambiguous: The genitive "nedelje" is the form "prošle/sledeće nedelje" ("last/next
nedelje") uses -- and dictionaries give "last WEEK" as the DEFAULT gloss of
that exact genitive (Wiktionary marks the weekday sense secondary at this
case; sr.wikipedia treats nedelja/sedmica as interchangeable for "week").
No source establishes one reading as dominant, so "prošle/sledeće nedelje"
refuses rather than silently picking the weekday sense (see
weekday_6.voc for the full disambiguation design).

gen pl).  Wiktionary, vek, declension table --
unit_day: "dan" syncretises genitive singular and genitive plural: "dva dana" (2-4)
and "pet dana" (5+) are both "dana".  Wiktionary, dan, declension table --
unit_decade: Full paradigm plus paucal: "dve decenije" (2-4, gen sg), "pet decenija"
(5+, gen pl).  Wiktionary, decenija, declension table --
unit_hour: Full paradigm: nominative singular (1), then the paucal rule -- 2-4
GENITIVE SINGULAR "sata", 5+ GENITIVE PLURAL "sati".  A naive gen.pl-only
reading mislabels "sata" as the paucal, which is wrong: it is the
genitive SINGULAR.  Wiktionary, sat, declension table --

surface: "dva minuta" (2-4, gen sg) and "pet minuta" (5+, gen pl) are both
unit_month: Full paradigm plus paucal: "dva meseca" (2-4, gen sg), "pet meseci" (5+,
gen pl).  Wiktionary, mesec, declension table --
unit_second: Full paradigm: nominative singular (1), then the paucal rule -- 2-4
GENITIVE SINGULAR, 5+ GENITIVE PLURAL -- "dve sekunde", "pet sekundi".

it also names Sunday and the two senses are not locally disambiguable in
a bare NUM+UNIT phrase.  Full paradigm plus paucal: "dve sedmice" (2-4,
gen sg), "pet sedmica" (5+, gen pl).  Wiktionary, sedmica, declension
unit_year: Full paradigm plus paucal: "dve godine" (2-4, gen sg), "pet godina" (5+,
